LESSON: READING 10.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.2: Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we relate events in a book to our own life experiences?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. respond to a text correctly for comprehension
2. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions such as proverbs, similes among others

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 10.2.1 INTENSIVE READING
This lesson teaches Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading for Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. respond to a text correctly for comprehension
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions such as proverbs, similes among others
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading above.
2. Explain Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we relate events in a book to our own life experiences?
2. How can you predict the information in a book even before you read it?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. respond to a text correctly for comprehension
2. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words and expressions such as proverbs, similes among others

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
